newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open steady, claims data awaited.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open steady, claims data awaited.

text.p: U.S. Treasury securities prices opened steady Thursday as players awaited initial jobless claims, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

Economists surveyed by Reuters expect, on average, that claims will rise to 341,000 in the week ended July 5, from 332,000 in the previous week. Any increase would be seen as favorable in the fixed-income markets due to the tightness of the U.S. labor market. As yet, wage pressures have been contained.
Should the numbers come in close to expectations, players will look to the Producer Price Index, due Friday. PPI is widely seen as being unchanged.
"The market's going to be a pancake today," said the head government trader at a primary dealership. "There's no key news coming out."
The market is at high levels and is likely to stay there a while, he said.
"PPI is what people are waiting for, but they already know we're in an inflation-friendly environment," the trader said.
It would take a surprising move in PPI to affect market price levels -- a plus or minus of more than 0.1 percent, he said.
PPI is due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT Friday.
There was some volatility in claims forecasts due to seasonal model turnover in the automobile industry, said Michael Englund, economist at MMS International.
Most of the concern about claims in recent weeks was dissipated by last week's tame employment report, he said.
On PPI, Englund looks for a decline of 0.1 percent, "so that's a good report."
With inflation contained and claims and PPI being the only important data of the week, the market's positive tone was set, he said.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was trading down 2/32 at 100-23/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
At the short end, three- and six-month bills were unchanged at 4.97 percent and 5.08 percent, respectively. Year bills were up one basis point at 5.24 percent.
Ten-year issues were down 1/32 at 102-21/32, yielding 6.26 percent. Five years were unchanged at 100-11/32 to yield 6.17 percent. Two-year notes were unchanged at 100-6/32 to yield 5.90 percent.
